plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated tempo run for speed development.
Incorporates hill work, a key component of trail running strength and efficiency.
Offers a more varied intensity profile to stimulate different physiological adaptations.
plan_b_advantages: Focuses on building a strong aerobic base with consistent easy runs.
Includes a strength and mobility session, which is beneficial for injury prevention and overall running form.
Has a slightly lower overall volume of running, potentially reducing the risk of overtraining for a runner who isn't already at a very high mileage level.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a more targeted approach to building race-relevant durability through a combination of longer runs at moderate intensity, hill work, and a tempo run – all crucial elements for trail racing. Plan B, while prioritizing endurance, lacks the specific intensity work needed to improve speed and relies heavily on extended, easy runs, which could lead to a plateau. Plan A’s structured progression feels more aligned with the goal of becoming a faster runner, while Plan B feels more geared towards simply covering distance.
